newsitem.title: UK: BBH will not re-pitch for Haagen-Dazs ad account.
newsitem.headline: BBH will not re-pitch for Haagen-Dazs ad account.

text.p: Bartle Bogle Hegarty, the London-based advertising agency which created ads for Haagen-Dazs ice cream emphasising its sensual pleasures, on Wednesday said it will not re-pitch for the Haagen-Dazs account.
BBH gave no reason for its decision. Agency officials were not available for comment.

"BBH is very proud of the world-famous advertising we have develped for Haagen-Dazs," BBH group director Julian Martin said in a statement. "It is now used by Pillsbury in Asia as well as Europe. We wish them well with their future agency."
Pillsbury Europe, part of Grand Metropolitan Plc, earlier had said it would conduct a full-service pitch review of the Haagen-Dazs advertisng account.

Pillsbury introduced Haagen-Dazs, a super-premium ice cream brand, to Europe in 1989. BBH was named to handle the initial UK advertising for Haagen-Dazs in 1990 and in 1991 launched the "seriously sensual" press ads for the brand. In 1992 and 1994 BBH re-pitched and won the pan-European Haagen-Dazs account.

Pillsbury officials could not be reached for comment on its decision to put the Haagen-Dazs account up for review. A spokeswoman said the company would not disclose the advertising agencies pitching for the account.

But the decision to put the account up for review follows the introduction of a new European brand management structure for Pillsbury's four brands, including Haagen-Dazs, Old El Paso, Green Giant and Pillsbury. Pillsbury UK managing director Martin Jamieson has said the company is looking to promote the ice cream brand with a single ad campaign across Europe.

BBH, in the statement announcing its decision, highlighted its achievements with the Haagen-Dazs account, noting that sales of the ice cream in 1991 -- the year of its first Haagen-Dazs ad campaign -- rose 398 percent over 1990 levels.
